title: Relative clauses and reference
subtitle: Trace the antecedent and the paragraph role together.
overview: A relative clause does more than translate “who” or “which”: it can identify, characterize, or develop a participant or claim already in the paragraph.
Its pronoun agrees with an antecedent in gender and number, but takes case from its own clause. Track both relationships.

sections.title: Two relationships
rows: antecedent: λόγος; object inside clause: ὃν
antecedent: ἀνήρ; recipient inside clause: ᾧ
relative clause as a named object of proclamation

items.grc: ὃ ἦν ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, ὃ ἀκηκόαμεν, ὃ ἑωράκαμεν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν.
items.en: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes.

items.grc: ὁ λόγος ὃν ἐλάλησα ἐκεῖνος κρινεῖ αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.
items.en: The word that I spoke will judge him on the last day.
